evidence: AddTaskUseCase, AssignTaskUseCase, CreateProjectUseCase, CreateUserUseCase, ListTasksUseCase and MarkTaskDoneUseCase all follow the same pattern: a repository injected through the constructor and a single execute() method.
MarkTaskDoneUseCase.execute asks the domain whether the task can be marked done (task.canMarkDone()) and then calls task.withStatus('done'), so the invariant stays in the domain.
AssignTaskUseCase.execute checks the user through UserRepository.getById, then calls task.withAssignee(assigneeId).
The 'Task with id ${taskId} not found' check appears in both AssignTaskUseCase.execute and MarkTaskDoneUseCase.execute. It is minor repeated boilerplate.
ProjectDTO, TaskDTO and UserDTO are declared, but no use case's execute() returns them. Each one returns a domain entity (Task, Project or User).
ListTasksUseCase.execute uses taskRepository.getByProjectIdAndAssignee in one branch but filters with tasks.filter(t => t.assigneeId === ...) in memory when both filters are set.
AddTaskUseCase.execute builds the Task with status 'todo' and a null assignee, so the starting state is set here.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The src/application module has one concern: application use cases for project, user and task management, plus the DTO shapes that go with them. Every use case follows the same pattern. Each one takes a domain repository interface through its constructor, exposes one execute() method, and passes domain entities in and out. Business invariants stay in the domain. MarkTaskDoneUseCase calls task.canMarkDone(), and the use cases use the immutable task.withStatus and task.withAssignee methods instead of changing fields directly. No use case reaches around the repository abstractions.

There are a few small issues, none serious enough to fail the module:
1. The "Task with id ... not found" lookup-and-throw logic is repeated in AssignTaskUseCase and MarkTaskDoneUseCase. This is boilerplate error handling, not a duplicated domain invariant.
2. ProjectDTO, TaskDTO and UserDTO are declared here, but no use case returns them. The use cases return the domain Task, Project and User types, so mapping to DTOs presumably happens in the infrastructure controllers. That is a boundary choice worth knowing about, but it is not a duplicated rule.
3. ListTasksUseCase filters by assignee in memory when both status and assignee filters are set. In the other branches it uses the repository query methods. The approach is mixed, but the rule still lives in one place.
4. AddTaskUseCase hard-codes the starting state of a new task (status 'todo', no assignee) when it builds the Task. This rule exists only in that one file.

None of these splits the module into unrelated concerns or puts an invariant in two places.
